To determine who caused the September 11, 2001 attacks, we look at the overwhelming consensus established by extensive investigations, most notably the official report by the 9/11 Commission. 

Step 1: Review historical evidence and official investigations. The 9/11 Commission Report, along with investigations by intelligence agencies and law enforcement worldwide, concluded that the terrorist attacks were planned and executed by the militant Islamist organization Al-Qaeda, led by Osama bin Laden.
Step 2: Evaluate the options against established historical facts. Options (A), (D), (E), and (F) represent various conspiracy theories lacking credible evidence. Options (B) and (G) attribute the attacks to foreign states that were not responsible. Option (C) accurately identifies the perpetrator group determined by international investigations.

Final answer: C
